correctness.rationale: The norm-saturation proof is correct. In logarithmic radial coordinates the m-th moment density has exponent F_M(u)=Mu-u^(3/2), with unique saddle u_M=4M^2/9 and peak 4M^3/27. The proposed disjoint shell boundaries are the neighboring saddles for M-1 and M+1, and their exponent deficits are exactly -4(3M-2)/27 and -4(3M+2)/27. Elementary monotonicity on the left and a tangent-tail bound on the right therefore show that the normalized m-th moment mass outside its assigned shell tends to zero exponentially. A shellwise-constant symbol hence interpolates every bounded target sequence modulo c0. For a fixed coordinate N, the scaled Jacobi polynomial supported in r<delta is orthogonal to all lower moments, normalizes the N-th moment to one, and satisfies a uniform tail bound C_{N,n} delta^(2(m-N)) for every m>N; thus e_N lies in the uniform closure. Closed linearity gives all c0 corrections, and combining the two constructions gives the entire ell-infinity sequence algebra. The homogeneous U(n)-decomposition is multiplicity-free with finite-dimensional blocks, so the commutant, compact ideal and quotient statements follow exactly as stated.

originality.rationale: Bdarneh's 2026 paper analyzes this logarithmic Fock weight and constructs a single alternating shell symbol to show that the classical square-root-metric sequence algebra fails. It does not state arbitrary bounded asymptotic interpolation, uniform recovery of c0, or full ell-infinity norm saturation. In the classical Gaussian Fock setting the radial Toeplitz algebra is the proper square-root-uniformly-continuous sequence algebra, and later constructive work concerns much smaller sequence classes. Searches by the exact weight, small-Fock terminology, full diagonal algebra and ell-infinity interpolation did not locate an equivalent prior theorem. The novelty is the exact norm-closed algebra identification for this weight.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a counterexample to a complete operator-algebra description: radial Toeplitz quantization is norm-dense in the full U(n)-commutant, with compact ideal c0 and corona ell-infinity/c0. This identifies an extreme small-Fock regime and provides two reusable mechanisms—saddle-separated shells and local moment probes—for testing norm saturation in other radial weights.

limitations: The theorem is specific to the displayed logarithmic weight and its flat unit-ball portion; it does not classify general radial Fock weights.
It proves norm density of eigenvalue sequences rather than surjectivity of the single-symbol map Lambda_n.
The local coordinate probes may require symbol norms growing as the localization radius tends to zero, so no uniformly bounded right inverse is claimed.
Only radial/U(n)-invariant Toeplitz operators are classified.
